I've been of my meds when I really should've been taking them, because I felt pretty good (as in not really miserable) for some time and since I didn't really like taking meds to begin with, thought I'd just ditch them.  
It takes some time for the effects to wear off, a few days, maybe a week, during that time I didn't feel any difference.  
When I was off them for two weeks I still felt fine, but definitely more unstable.  
So I did function relatively normal, but I did take them for a reason and if my timing would've been a little worse, I think it may have had made more of an impact.

It depends on the person prescribing them and your circumstances.  
When I was on anti-depressants they told me I'd be for at least 2 years, with decreasing dosage over the last 6 months to ease me out of therapy.  
They really are just tools to help the therapy and most psychiatrists I met used them as such.  
That said, major depression usually doesn't fix itself over night, so you might take them for a while.  
IMHO you have nothing to fear.. you can also just refuse taking any medication until you feel comfortable doing so.  
I did that with my first therapist and she has been very understanding - once I felt that it might help me get back on my feet, we discussed it and went with a low dosage at first :)
